scope: Entities were reviewed across October 19–21. October 21 adds conservative guides and local roster checks. Individual evidence dates remain attached to claims. This is not a claim that all Oregon endorsers or every private decision are captured.

entities.name: AG-PAC
entities.review: All 42 candidates on the checked 2026 list included. Source does not specify primary versus general stage.

entities.name: Animal Wellness Action
entities.review: All seven Oregon candidates in the checked 2026 national list included.

entities.name: Associated General Contractors Oregon-Columbia Chapter
entities.review: One current campaign-reported endorsement located after the official advocacy-page review, all 22 state November pamphlets and the campaign-page sweep. Greg Smith’s page labels its list Previous Endorsements, so it was not added as a 2026 endorsement. No full current issuer slate was located; the count is documented public claims, not proof that the organization endorsed only one candidate.

entities.name: Centrist Independent Voter / CIVPAC
entities.review: Checked the full 2026 general-election House, Senate and governor directories. Merkley is the only endorsed Oregon candidate there. Oregon CD5 is marked Under Review rather than endorsed; it is excluded. No Oregon governor endorsement appears. The short Oregon list is consistent with these published directories.

entities.name: Deschutes County Republican Party
entities.review: Reviewed the full October 17 general-election page, including its linked candidate cards. Fifteen clearly featured candidate listings and the Yes on Measure 9-185 position are included. Raun Atkinson appears only below Do your research, so that mention is not counted as support. Raven Hanson in the party page is matched to Raven Hansen in the county pamphlet using the same Redmond council contest and campaign context.

entities.name: Food & Water Action
entities.review: The checked current page lists Jeff Merkley for Oregon; included.

entities.name: JStreetPAC
entities.review: All four Oregon candidates in the checked current national directory included: Merkley, Bonamici, Hoyle and Salinas. Profiles identify endorsements but do not specify election stage. The short list is not inferred from Merkley’s page alone.

entities.name: Jane Fonda Climate PAC / JanePAC
entities.review: Current 2026 Oregon entries captured where matched to November candidates. Tonia Moro is outside the checked November SD3 roster. Older 2022/2024/2025 entries excluded.

entities.name: Kaarin Knudson
entities.review: Expanded through explicit November campaign statements and current campaign endorsement lists. Undated current pages are marked stage unspecified; historical lists, references to employment and criticism of opponents are excluded. This person has no verified central public slate, so the included count is documented campaign claims rather than an exhaustive list of personal decisions.

entities.name: Kevin Mannix
entities.review: Expanded through explicit November campaign statements and current campaign endorsement lists. Undated current pages are marked stage unspecified; historical lists, references to employment and criticism of opponents are excluded. This person has no verified central public slate, so the included count is documented campaign claims rather than an exhaustive list of personal decisions.

entities.name: Kim Thatcher
entities.review: Expanded through explicit November campaign statements and current campaign endorsement lists. Undated current pages are marked stage unspecified; historical lists, references to employment and criticism of opponents are excluded. This person has no verified central public slate, so the included count is documented campaign claims rather than an exhaustive list of personal decisions.

entities.name: Kitty Piercy
entities.review: Expanded through explicit November campaign statements and current campaign endorsement lists. Undated current pages are marked stage unspecified; historical lists, references to employment and criticism of opponents are excluded. This person has no verified central public slate, so the included count is documented campaign claims rather than an exhaustive list of personal decisions.

entities.name: LCV Action Fund
entities.review: All six Oregon candidates returned by the current 2026 General state filter included.

entities.name: Lookout Eugene-Springfield editorial board
entities.review: Reviewed the four October 14–17 general-election editorials: legislative, federal/governor, city/county and measures. Conditional clean-energy support is described in the card.

entities.name: NFIB FedPAC
entities.review: Both Oregon candidates in the September 23 announcement included.

entities.name: NFIB OR PAC
entities.review: All 37 candidates in the August 3 legislative announcement included, plus the separately sourced Drazan endorsement. State committee kept separate from FedPAC.

entities.name: NRDC Action Fund
entities.review: Current 2026 Oregon panel checked: Maxine Dexter and Jeff Merkley. Prior-year panels were excluded.

entities.name: Oregon AFSCME
entities.review: State and local issuer page reviewed; added Sean VanGordon after a November roster check and two additional explicit November campaign claims (Mark Gamba and Jason Kropf). Metro entries still require November roster resolution. Paul Savas and Catherine McMullen were matched to the official November county list on October 21. Jasmine Hatmaker and Tai Pruce-Zimmerman are absent from the checked November Eugene roster. Mai Vang / Salem Ward 6 conflicts with it. Local-union-only claims were not assigned to the statewide council.

entities.name: Oregon Coalition of Police & Sheriffs
entities.review: 36 candidate-reported endorsements captured after reviewing all 22 state November pamphlets and current campaign pages. Official homepage and PAC page do not supply a full public slate. Page/column notes identify pamphlet claims. A compromised campaign page was excluded as new evidence. These are campaign claims, not issuer confirmation or a claim that every ORCOPS decision is public.

entities.name: Oregon Consumer League Action Fund
entities.review: Full general-election list reviewed. Teresa Alonso Leon / SD11 withheld because the November roster names Virginia Stapleton; Christina Stephenson was elected in the primary and is outside this November guide.

entities.name: Oregon Education Association PAC
entities.review: All 51 names in the checked tables included. The five federal entries are recommendations to NEA, not endorsements.

entities.name: Oregon Farm Bureau
entities.review: 20 explicit campaign-reported endorsements captured from November pamphlet statements. The official homepage/advocacy pages do not supply a complete current public slate. Employment references and undated Previous Endorsements pages were excluded. Farm Bureau remains distinct from AG-PAC.

entities.name: Oregon Firearms Federation PAC
entities.review: The June 1, 2026 issuer report explicitly identifies PAC endorsements of Jack Tibbetts and Ken Jackola. Dwayne Yunker’s November statement explicitly names the PAC. These three are included, with primary and general evidence distinguished. Glenn Lancaster’s generic parent-organization reference is not assigned to the PAC. No complete November issuer slate was located.

entities.name: Oregon Labor Federation, AFL-CIO
entities.review: Full federal/state slate and chapter recommendations reviewed. Added five local choices after official November checks: Sean VanGordon, Cathie Rigby, Thaddeus Betz, Victoria Slaboda and Jack Buckley. John Wilson and Isabella Lee Tibbetts were also added after checking the official November county pamphlets; all names in the checked candidate list are now accounted for. Chapter recommendations are identified in notes rather than described as an additional statewide committee vote.

entities.name: Oregon League of Conservation Voters
entities.review: 105 of 106 published positions included. Mai Vang / Salem Ward 6 withheld because the certified November roster lists Betsy Vega.

entities.name: Oregon Nurses Association PAC
entities.review: All 60 roster-matched candidates from the checked official 2026 list included, including Samuel Denney after a Roseburg election-office check. Added a separate campaign-reported Cyrus Javadi claim from his November statement; 61 total. The city lists Ellen Porter as withdrawn, so she is excluded.

entities.name: Oregon Right to Life PAC
entities.review: Reviewed the issuer’s 2026 primary-winners article, all 22 state November pamphlets and current campaign endorsement pages. Primary claims remain labeled Primary; a November campaign statement does not become issuer confirmation. The full current LifeVote guide requires an address and does not offer a public statewide export in the pages checked. May-elected county candidates are not imported as November contests.

entities.name: Oregon State Fire Fighters Council
entities.review: All 57 candidates on the official one-page general-election poster included.

entities.name: Oregon Working Families Party
entities.review: Full Our Candidates table reconciled to covered November rosters; all ten previously missing local names added after checking election-office November records. Cannon Beach’s latest linked notice is a filing list, so its final certified ballot check remains pending. Christina Stephenson was elected in the primary. Additional supported local measures still need ballot-identity checks. Party-listed support is distinguished from nomination.

entities.name: Oregonians for Food & Shelter
entities.review: All 39 candidates in the guide’s own endorsement panels included. Comparisons of other organizations are not treated as primary confirmation of those organizations.

entities.name: Our Revolution
entities.review: Current national Our Champions directory and linked Oregon slate reviewed. Merkley, Carpenter and Nelson retain primary-cycle evidence; Wasielewski and Osborne are not November candidates. Added Charles Maughan’s explicitly national campaign-reported endorsement. Corvallis Allies chapter endorsements are not assigned to the national organization.

entities.name: Peace Action
entities.review: The checked current Oregon section lists Jeff Merkley; included.

entities.name: Planned Parenthood Action Fund
entities.review: Current Oregon congressional panel checked: all six candidates included. This is separate from Oregon’s state PAC.

entities.name: Planned Parenthood Action Oregon
entities.review: 65 Oregon state/local endorsements included from the union of the official general-election web table (64 names) and four-page PDF. Travis Nelson appears in the PDF on page 2; Amy Sabbadini and Julia Brim-Edwards appear on the web table. Federal endorsements belong to the separate national Action Fund.

entities.name: Population Connection Action Fund
entities.review: The checked 2026 page lists Jeff Merkley for Oregon; included.

entities.name: Portland for All voter guide
entities.review: All explicitly presented current candidate/measure positions captured after adding Steph Routh from Other Key Races and the certified conservation-district roster. Christina Stephenson is outside the November contest roster. Broad referrals to WFP are not copied as Portland for All endorsements.

entities.name: SEIU Oregon State Council
entities.review: Full general-election page reviewed plus two explicit November campaign claims for Jennifer Smith and Athena Aguiar. R W Smith is still withheld because the issuer names Clackamas City Council, creating an office/identity conflict with the county commission race.

entities.name: Sierra Club - National
entities.review: All five Oregon candidates in the checked 2026 national federal directory included: Merkley, Bonamici, Beck, Dexter and Salinas. The directory does not list Hoyle or Bynum for Oregon. Election stage is unspecified. This is a separate published directory; it does not imply five independent decisions in addition to chapter decisions.

entities.name: Sierra Club Oregon Chapter
entities.review: All 52 positions on the checked Oregon Chapter November list included: 49 candidates and three measures. Kept separate from the national federal directory. An ambiguous generic Sierra Club campaign claim was removed rather than assigned to a committee without evidence.

entities.name: Stand for Health Freedom
entities.review: All 22 rows in the issuer’s October 20 general-election PDF were reconciled: 21 November candidates included, with G Mark Norman labeled Recommended. Jason Fields’s county commission race was decided in May; the official November Yamhill county-candidate table lists only clerk candidates. That row is excluded from November listings. Candidate names are matched using their current official November races.

entities.name: Taxpayers Association of Oregon
entities.review: Captured explicit November pamphlet and current campaign claims plus the association’s bylined No on Hillsboro Measure 34-355 statement, linked from its official news site. No complete current public candidate slate was found. Campaign claims are labeled Campaign-reported; older taxpayer guides are excluded.

entities.name: The Corvallis Advocate
entities.review: Expanded the candidate and school-levy editorial, with first/second ranking choices identified. Its Ward 1 discussion explicitly declines an endorsement. The separate charter-measure editorial remains a source to review.

entities.name: The Mother PAC
entities.review: May primary slate and current public news reviewed. Matching primary claims retain their cycle labels; November pamphlet evidence and current campaign reports bring included records to 10. A general-election issuer slate was not found. Old sections on Thuy Tran and Andrea Valderrama pages were not imported as 2026 endorsements; rescinded Teresa Alonso Leon support is not counted.

entities.name: Umatilla County Republican Central Committee
entities.review: All seven candidates on the official November slate included after county-roster checks. The party’s Cliff Bentz entry says District 1; the official election roster establishes District 2. The candidate is unambiguous, so the endorsement is retained with that discrepancy disclosed in the card.

entities.name: Union Contractor Group
entities.review: One explicit current campaign claim located in the November pamphlet sweep. No separate current issuer slate was verified. The Union Contractor Group is not merged with Associated General Contractors. The count does not establish how many non-public decisions the group made.

entities.name: Val Hoyle
entities.review: Expanded through explicit November campaign statements and current campaign endorsement lists. Undated current pages are marked stage unspecified; historical lists, references to employment and criticism of opponents are excluded. This person has no verified central public slate, so the included count is documented campaign claims rather than an exhaustive list of personal decisions.

entities.name: Willamette Week editorial board
entities.review: Reviewed all seven linked fall sections, including legislative, city, county and judicial choices. Ranking order is explained in the cards. No endorsement is inferred from a person merely being discussed.

researchPass.method: Full published issuer lists plus manually reviewed campaign statements; name mentions alone are not endorsements. Old election sections, opponent criticism, employment references and contributions are excluded.

claim.note: Campaign-submitted voters’ pamphlet statement. Election office hosts but does not verify the endorsement.

retiredClaims.reason: Campaign said Sierra Club without identifying the issuing committee. Not assigned to either national or Oregon chapter.
